column2: You sent the ripened milk into the raw, you raised the Sun in heaven; heat the Saman like the hot milk with fair praises, the great song pleasing to the lover of hymns.
Your great, delighting exhilaration, O bay-horsed, has been drunk like a cup; your drop, the bull's, is a racer, the best winner of thousands.
May your delighting, bull-like, choice exhilaration come to us, Indra, strong, victorious, conquering armies, immortal.
For you are a hero, the winner; urge the chariot of Manu; strong, you burned the lawless Dasyu like a vessel with flame.
Flow us rain, the wave of waters from heaven, and great strengths free from disease.
Flow with that stream by which the cows came here, the folk to our house.
Flow ghee with the stream, best at the gods' feast in the sacrifices; flow rain to us.
For strength, run through the woolen filter with the stream; the gods hear for happiness.
Flowing, he ran, smiting the demons, making the lights shine as of old.
Come to him with the somas, the best soma-drinker; with cups, the master of the residue, Indra, with the pressed drops.
If you adorn him with the pressed drops, the somas — the wise knower of all seeks him the bold one.
For him alone bring the pressed stalk, Adhvaryu; often he has given voice against the curse of the victorious one who strives.
Sing a song to Soma, the brown, self-strong, ruddy, touching heaven.
Cleanse the pressed soma with stones released from the hand; run, honey-bearer, run, honey.
With homage sit near; with curds mix; place the drop in Indra.
Foe-slayer, all-seeing, flow, Soma, for the welfare of the cow, fulfilling the wishes of the gods.
For Indra to drink, Soma, you are poured around for exhilaration, the mind, lord of mind.
Flowing one, give us wealth with heroic strength, Soma; O drop, with Indra as our ally.
You rise, O Sun, toward the famed bounteous bull, the man of good works, the archer.
Who by the strength of his arm split ninety-nine forts, and the Vritra-slayer slew the serpent.
That Indra is our kind friend, with horses, cattle and barley; he milks like a wide stream.
May the shining, great one drink the honeyed soma, giving unharmed life to the lord of the sacrifice; urged by the wind, he guards by himself, nourishes offspring, and shines in many ways.
The shining, great, well-borne, best winner of strength, the truth set in heaven's support; foe-slayer, Vritra-slayer, best Dasyu-slayer, the light was born, slayer of Asuras, slayer of rivals.
This best light of lights, highest, all-conquering, wealth-winning, great, is said; all-shining, the great Sun, to be seen, has spread wide with unshaken power.
Bring us wisdom, Indra, as a father to his sons; teach us in this course, O much-invoked, that living we may attain the light.
Let neither unknown crookednesses and evil thoughts nor the inauspicious overcome us; with you, O hero, we cross the eternal waters over the slopes.
Today and tomorrow, Indra, save us, and on the far days; O lord of the good, protect all our singers, by day and night.
The breaker, hero, bounteous, of much bounty, mingled for heroism; both your arms, O hundred-powered, are bull-like, holding the thunderbolt.
Desiring women, desiring sons, good givers, we call Sarasvati.
And may Sarasvati, dearest of the dear, sister of seven, well-pleased, be to be praised by us.
We meditate on that choicest radiance of the god Savitar, who may urge on our thoughts.
Make the soma-sounds ring, O Brahmanaspati, for Kakshivan, the son of Ushij.
O Agni, you purify our lives; bring us energy and food; drive far away evil dogs.
Make us able for the great earthly and heavenly wealth; great is your power among the gods.
By truth they follow truth and attain the swift skill; the two unharming gods grow strong.
The rain-bringers, flowing, lords of strength, from the giver's cloud, attain the vast chasm.
They yoke the ruddy, moving one, the bay, around the standing; the lights shine in heaven.
His two dear bay horses are yoked, with side-wings, on the chariot, red, bold, bearing men.
Making a banner for the bannerless, form for the formless, O men, you were born with the dawns.
This soma, Indra, is pressed for you, flows for you; protect it; you who have made it, you who have rained the drop for friendly exhilaration.
That chariot like a carrier of burdens is yoked for the winning of many great treasures; then all the human clans, born, in the winning of heaven, have bowed the woods high.
Strong, like the Marut host in strength, flow free from blame, as the divine people; like waters, be swiftly favorable to us; thousandfold-working, like a sacrifice that overcomes armies.
With your joyful tongues at the sacrifice, worship the great ones for us; bring the gods and worship.
For you know, O ordainer, the ways and paths of the gods directly, Agni, at sacrifices, skilful one.
The priest, the immortal god, goes before with skill, urging on the rites.
The racer is set among strengths, led forward at sacrifices, the sage, accomplisher of the rite.
By thought he made the choice; he placed the embryo of beings; father of skill, by his extension.
Pour out the glory at the pressing, the glory of both worlds; with essences let them hold the bull.
They know their own home, like calves with their mothers; they are joined together with their kin.
In the ladles, those who toil make the support in heaven; to Indra and Agni homage, heaven.
That indeed was the eldest in the worlds, whence fierce, bright-mannered you were born; being born, at once he strikes enemies, in whom all the helpers rejoice.
Growing by strength, of abundant vigor, the enemy puts fear into the Dasa; sounding and unsounding, the winner; they sing you at the carrying in the joys.
In you all choose skill, when these helpers become twice and thrice; with the sweet make it sweeter, with sweet honey fight with honey.

In the Trikadrukas the great one, of great strength, satisfied, drank the soma pressed with Vishnu, as he wished; he rejoiced to perform the great deed; the true god-drop, the true Indra, joins the great, wide god.

Born together with skill, together with might you have carried, grown together with powers, conqueror of enemies, all-seeing; giver of bounty, desirable wealth to the praiser, O wise; the true god-drop, the true Indra, joins the great god.

Then, brilliant, by might you overcame in battle the active; you filled both worlds by your power and grew great; you placed the other in your belly; he passed; awaken; the true god-drop, the true Indra, joins the great god.
Praise Indra, lord of cattle, with song as one who knows — son of truth, lord of the good.
The bay horses have been yoked on the red grass where we sing together.
The cows milked a mixture for Indra the thunderbolt-bearer, honey, which he found in the fold.
You are the first giver of bounties, true, maker of rulers; we choose the associate of the much-splendid son of great power.
The ancient, first nectar, the praiseworthy, the great one entered heaven and milked it; they sang together to Indra being born.
Then some, seeing their kin, the heavenly ones of wealthy radiance, praised; Savitar uncovers the choice of heaven.
And when, flowing, these two worlds and all these worlds by your might — like a bull in a herd you shine forth.
You are divided, O wondrous-splendored one, near the wave of the river; at once you flow to the giver.
Bring us a share in the highest and middle strengths; teach us the nearest of the wealth.
By ancient birth I adorn songs like Kanva, by which Indra took strength.
The sages who did not praise you, Indra, and those who did — grow strong, well-praised, in my song.
Agni, with all fires, accept the prayer, O born of strength; with those among the gods and among the Ayus, magnify our songs.
Forth with all the fires is that Agni whose racer is — for offspring and children, from us, surrounded by strengths together.
You, Agni, with fires, increase our prayer and sacrifice; urge us for the gods' feast, for giving wealth.
In you, Soma, the grass-strewers first set thought for great strength and fame; you, hero, urge us to heroism.
You have crossed over with glory like a fountain, an unfailing drink for the people; bearing in the hands like arrows.
You, immortal, have begotten for the mortal, in the law of the immortal, of the lovely immortal; ever running, going to win strength.
I spoke to the lord of the bay horses, who fills with bounty; now hear, the praiser of the horse-giver.
For never before was one born more heroic than you; neither by wealth nor by help nor by joy.
The bull of you who give, the bull of you who unite; you urge the lord of the milch-cows.
May the god, giver of wealth, bring you the full pouring-vessel; pour it out or fill it up — then the god carries it on to you.
The gods made him the priest of the sacrifice, the wise carrier; Agni bestows jewels, heroic strength, on the giver.
From whom the peoples tremble when he does terrible deeds — worship Agni, winner of thousands, with thoughts as in the winning of wisdom.
O Agni, you purify our lives; bring us energy and food; drive far away evil dogs.
Agni is the sage, the flowing, of the five peoples, the household priest; we ask for him of great house.
Agni, flow, of good works; bring us splendor and heroic strength, setting wealth upon me and a maid.
Agni, purifier, with joyful flame, god, with the tongue, bring the gods and worship.
That ghee-bathed one we call, O wonder-radiant, seeing heaven; bring the gods for the feast.
We kindle you, seer, of the feast offering, radiant, great, at the sacrifice, Agni.
Protect us, Agni, with help in the Gayatri offering; to be praised in all thoughts.
Bring us wealth, Agni, ever-victorious, choice, hard to overcome in all battles.
Bring us, Agni, with fair wisdom, wealth that nourishes the whole life; place comfort for our living.
Let our thoughts urge Agni, like a swift horse in the races; by him may we win wealth after wealth.
By whatever army, Agni, with your help we gain cattle — urge that on us for bounty.
Bring, Agni, solid wealth, wide, with cattle and horses; open the space, drive the wheel-rim.
Agni, you made the ageless star, the Sun, rise in heaven, giving light to the people.
Agni, you are the banner of the clans, dearest, best, seated near; awaken and give vigor to the praiser.
You rule over desirable gifts, Agni, lord of heaven; may I be the praiser in your shelter.
Up, Agni, your bright pure flames rise shining; your light-rays.
Who is your kinsman among the people, Agni? Who is a sacrificer? Who, in what do you rest?
You are the kinsman of the people, Agni; you are dear Mitra, a friend to be praised among friends.
Worship Mitra and Varuna for us; worship the gods and the great truth; Agni, worship your own house.
To be praised, to be revered, driving away darkness, beautiful, the bull Agni is kindled.
The bull Agni is kindled like a horse that carries the gods; with offering they praise him.
We kindle you, the bull, O bull; Agni, shine greatly.
Your great flames of the kindled, brilliant one rise, Agni, bright ones.
Let my ladles come to you with ghee, beloved; Agni, accept our offerings.
I praise Agni, joyful priest, seasonal, wondrous-radiant, shining with riches; may he hear.
Protect us from every demon, ungenerous; help us in battles; for you, nearest, we, O friend, reach for the gods' feast, for growth.
O king, the unfriendly one kindled is seen, fierce, for skill, well pressed; he shines with great light and goes to the ruddy bright one, driving away the black.
When he appeared in form to the dark mare, begetting the woman, sister of the great father, raising the Sun's light on high, he shines with the Vasus of heaven.
The auspicious came joining the auspicious, the lover goes after the sister; Agni stands apart with bright days, with shining colors, and has stood toward the dark.
With what praise, Agni Angiras, grandson of strength, shall I choose for you, god, a great fury?
In what mind shall we give for the sacrifice, O son of strength? What shall I say, this homage?
